target.title: fix(agents): preserve heartbeat CLI session bindings
target.body:
Closes #98895

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where heartbeat turns for Claude CLI-backed sessions could advance the CLI conversation into a new session id while leaving OpenClaw's stored session binding pointed at the pre-heartbeat id. The next user turn could then resume stale CLI context and lose everything the heartbeat turn learned or did.

## Why This Change Was Made

Session usage persistence now separates display-model preservation from CLI binding persistence. Heartbeat and runtime-model-preserving runs still keep the user-visible model fields stable, but they can persist a new CLI session binding or clear a stale unflushed binding; only explicitly user-facing-state-preserving internal updates continue to skip CLI binding mutations.

## User Impact

Claude CLI-backed agents keep conversation continuity across heartbeat turns. Heartbeats no longer orphan a new CLI session on disk while the next user turn resumes the older pre-heartbeat session.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: heartbeat session usage updates preserve the displayed session model while still writing a replacement Claude CLI binding or clearing a stale unflushed binding.
- Commands:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts -- --reporter=dot`
  - `git diff --check`
  - `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local`
- Observed result:
  - Focused Vitest: 1 file passed, 125 tests passed.
  - `git diff --check`: passed.
  - Autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings reported; overall patch is correct (0.87). The autoreview wrapper printed a late Windows GBK decode exception after the clean verdict, but the actionable review result completed and reported no findings.
- Not tested / proof gaps:
  - No live Claude CLI heartbeat run was executed in this Windows worktree; validation is focused source-level regression coverage for the persistence boundary identified in the issue.
